Learning model fitted to Middleton, Rawson & Verkuilen (2019): 4 participants, 192 items each, retrieval practice vs repetition x spaced (lag 24) vs massed (lag 1), four sessions, tests at 7 and 28 days. Simulation of the published protocol; binomial likelihood on 56 observed cells.

Shared parameters: c = 0.201, alpha = 0.139, s = 0.251, tau = -0.70 (fixed); trace weights: successful retrieval 1.00 (scale), failed retrieval + feedback 0.59, study 0.58. Per participant baseline beta: P1 -1.18, P2 -1.41, P3 -1.84, P4 -1.46. Negative log-likelihood 1721.

What the fit captures: the spacing effect at both delays, the retrieval-practice advantage at both delays, the rise across sessions, and the forgetting between 7 and 28 days; the worst pooled cell is off by 0.08. What it does not: individual differences in the retrieval-practice effect. P3 shows the reverse pattern and P4 an unusually large advantage; a shared model with only a per-participant baseline cannot produce either, and a per-participant learning scale was not identifiable from four participants. Treat the trace weights as population averages.

Assumptions: sessions on days 0, 3, 7, 10; 12 s per trial; the within-training measure is the first attempt of sessions 2-4; tau fixed at Pavlik & Anderson (2005)'s value; items start at a retrieval probability of 0.03 before training (they were selected as unnameable); the power law runs in seconds with a one-second floor.
